artifact.name: followup-04-cell-boundary
artifact.title: Cell lifecycle boundary observation
artifact.clean_room_rule: Ghidra observations are static evidence from SporeApp.exe; imported names and decompiler types are bounded evidence, not a claim of complete original runtime truth.

scope.question: Whether cCellGFX/mGFXObjectIndex can detach and rebuild while retaining the same cCellObjectData/pool identity, and how cCellGame+0x411c, cCellObjectData+0x108, and cCellObjectData+0x248 behave across creation, despawn, reload, OnExit, and Dispose.

verdict.headline: A static in-place per-cell GFX association seam exists, but no single straight-line invocation was proven to detach and rebuild the association while retaining the same cell. The same cell/pool identity is retained across the separate detach and rebuild branches; despawn and stage reload are identity-destructive.
verdict.positive_path: FUN_00e7c8c0 -> FUN_00e78c00 -> (FUN_00e66010 detach when +0x248 is present) or (FUN_00e6d8f0 rebuild when +0x248 is absent) -> FUN_00e5ce90 initializes the new GFX record
verdict.positive_path_limit: The detach and rebuild calls are mutually exclusive branches of FUN_00e78c00. The evidence supports same identity across separate per-cell operations, not an atomic detach-then-rebuild transaction or a runtime guarantee.
negative_paths: FUN_00e780a0 detaches/releases GFX state and then always releases the input cCellObjectData pool object.
FUN_00e7fd00 clears sCellGame+0x411c, drains the cell pool, detaches GFX records, and releases the old cCellObjectData pool objects before setup/population work.
verdict.modern_invariant: Use a stable simulation CellId/pool identity independent of an optional, replaceable GFX association index; keep content references, gameplay state, GFX/UI state, and serializable save state in separate ownership domains.
verdict.recovered_original_behavior: The original uses a cell pool index as simulation identity and a separate GFX pool index at cCellObjectData+0x248. The original also has a per-cell detach/rebuild seam, but its despawn and stage-rebuild helpers release the old cell object rather than preserving it.

cCellGFX.cell_gfx_record_note: The imported structure names the pool but does not expose a complete cCellGFX::CellGFXObjectData layout. The record's reciprocal cell association is recovered from FUN_00e6d8f0/FUN_00e5ce90 and from FUN_00e66010's pool accesses.

creation.name: Simulator::Cell::CreateCellObject
observations: Allocates a cObjectPoolIndex from the cell pool.
Initializes transform, orientation, size, scale, health, query, and gameplay fields.
Calls GetModelKeyForCellResource and writes the resulting ResourceKey to cCellObjectData+0xfc.
Writes the cCellDataReference<cCellCellResource>* to cCellObjectData+0x108.
The direct create body does not establish the later GFX association write; the observed writer of +0x248 is FUN_00e6d8f0.

creation.name: Simulator::Cell::GetModelKeyForCellResource
observations: Resolves the cCellDataReference before inspecting the resource's model-key table.
Can derive a key from resource records or the current serializable-data player key.
The returned ResourceKey is copied into cCellObjectData+0xfc by CreateCellObject.

per_cell_gfx_detach.name: FUN_00e66010
observations: The implicit EAX input is a cCellObjectData pool index; disassembly uses the cCellGame cell pool at sCellGame+0x1c.
Reads cCellObjectData+0x248 and resolves that index through cCellGFX.mCellGFXObjects at sCellGFX+0x168.
Writes zero to cCellObjectData+0x248.
Invokes FUN_00e65ad0 on the GFX record and then releases the GFX record pool entry.
Does not release the cCellObjectData pool entry itself.

per_cell_gfx_rebuild.name: FUN_00e6d8f0
observations: Resolves the existing cCellObjectData from param_1 through the cell pool.
Allocates a new GFX object through FUN_00b72160.
Writes the new GFX pool index to puVar3[0x92], which is cCellObjectData+0x248.
Calls FUN_00e5ce90 with the new GFX index and the existing cell's mObjectPoolIndex; FUN_00e5ce90 writes the cell index to the GFX record at +0x0c.
Replays idle animation on the same cCellObjectData and does not release the cell object.
The only direct xref to FUN_00e6d8f0 is the +0x248==0 branch of FUN_00e78c00.

detached_branch.condition: FUN_00e5cde0 returns nonzero and the cell has a nonzero +0x248 GFX index
detached_branch.call: FUN_00e66010 with the same cell pool index

rebuilt_branch.condition: FUN_00e78c00 reaches its non-detach path with cCellObjectData+0x248 == 0

positive_same_identity_seam.interpretation: The same cCellObjectData/pool identity can be the owner before and after a per-cell GFX association is detached and later reattached. The two operations are separate conditional branches, not a proven single-call sequence.

despawn.name: FUN_00e780a0
observations: Resolves param_1 as a cCellObjectData pool index.
If it equals sCellGame+0x411c, clears the avatar index to zero.
Removes the cell from query/linked state and releases related query handles.
If +0x248 is nonzero, detaches the GFX record through FUN_00e66010.
When the scale-replacement mode is active, calls FUN_00e67890 and may call FUN_00e771d0 using the old cell's +0x108 resource reference and +0xfc model key to populate replacement/child cells.
Always calls FUN_00b72260(param_1) after the conditional work, releasing the input cCellObjectData pool object.
There are 27 xrefs from 23 caller functions, including death, interaction, population, and setup/rebuild helpers.
despawn.identity_result: The GFX association is detached in place as an intermediate operation, but the old cCellObjectData identity is not retained after the helper returns. Any replacement is a newly created/selected object, not the same pool record.

stage_reload.name: FUN_00e7fd00
observations: Clears sCellGame+0x51d8 and sCellGame+0x411c.
Drains the transient interaction list through FUN_00e7e130.
Iterates the cell pool, clears a matching avatar index, detaches +0x248 through FUN_00e66010, and releases each cCellObjectData pool object with FUN_00b72260.
Drains GFX/effect/UI state and resets world/scale/setup state before population/setup work.
Reads mode fields from cCellSerializableData at cCellGame+0x5190 and writes them into the serializable object during setup.
stage_reload.identity_result: No old cCellObjectData/pool identity is retained across the reload drain. This is a rebuild of runtime state, not a same-cell visual refresh.

mode_exit.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::OnExit
observations: Restores global display/background values.
Drains and releases transient interaction records through FUN_00e7e130.
Calls FUN_00e64a00, which drains cCellGFX preloaded/visual records and presentation handles, resets the shadow/light/model/effect services, and resets UI state.
Calls FUN_00e82d40 for additional service cleanup.
The direct body has no cCellObjectData+0x108, +0x248, or sCellGame+0x411c field rewrite and no cCellObjectData pool release.
mode_exit.identity_result: OnExit is a mode/presentation cleanup boundary. It does not itself prove either retention or destruction of the cell pool; that distinction belongs to the subsequent stage reload or service Dispose path.

mode_dispose.name: App::cCellModeStrategy::Dispose
observations: Performs mode-specific conditional cleanup and GFX world cleanup.
Calls FUN_00e63f90 for cCellGame, FUN_00e64090 for cCellGFX, and FUN_00e61b00 for cCellUI through separate service bodies.
FUN_00e64090 releases cCellGFX world/layer/model/effect/preload handles and the GFX object pool storage.
FUN_00e61b00 releases UI layout/rollover state.
FUN_00e63f90 releases cCellGame-owned runtime/service state through generic pool/refcount cleanup; its direct body does not explicitly rewrite +0x411c, +0x108, or +0x248.
mode_dispose.identity_result: Dispose is a deeper owner/service release boundary than OnExit. It is not an in-place GFX association rebuild.

serializable_state.constructor: 0x00e61550 allocates 0xec bytes and installs serializable/refcount vtables; 0x00e61630 initializes mode/player/resource-related state around that constructor.
serializable_state.ownership: cCellGame+0x5190 holds mpSerializableData; cCellGame::Initialize allocates or adopts it, and cCellGame::Initialize xrefs the global serializable slot.
serializable_state.handoff: FUN_00e63d10 allocates a new 0xec object, swaps it into Simulator::Cell::sCellSerializableData, and copies state through FUN_00e627a0. FUN_00e819b0 can similarly adopt/swap the global object before cCellGame::Initialize.
serializable_state.save_candidate_classification: Explicit mode-specific serializable state candidate, separate from cCellObjectData gameplay state, cCellGFX/cCellUI presentation, and Cell content records. This pass did not observe a disk transaction and does not claim one.

field_ownership_and_classification.modern_invariant: The association is optional and replaceable; it is not the simulation identity.

The key is separate from the GFX index at +0x248
field_ownership_and_classification.modern_invariant: Model/content key is not presentation state and should not be discarded merely because a GFX association is rebuilt.
Gameplay state belongs to the simulation identity and survives a presentation detach/rebuild when the cell is not despawned.

hypotheses.name: in_place_gfx_association_seam
hypotheses.claim: A cCellObjectData pool identity can survive a per-cell GFX association detach and later reattach.
predictions: A detach helper must clear cCellObjectData+0x248 without calling the cell pool release on its input cell index.
A rebuild helper must receive an existing cCellObjectData and write a newly allocated GFX index to +0x248.
The caller must continue using the same cell object after the rebuild helper returns.
evidence: FUN_00e66010 clears +0x248 and releases the GFX record, not the cell record.
FUN_00e6d8f0 resolves the existing cell, allocates a GFX record, writes +0x248, and calls PlayAnimation on the same cell.
FUN_00e7c8c0 iterates the cell pool and invokes FUN_00e78c00 without releasing the loop cell in the positive branch.

hypotheses.name: single_call_atomic_detach_rebuild
hypotheses.claim: One recovered function unconditionally detaches and rebuilds the GFX association while retaining the same cell identity.
predictions: The same function would call FUN_00e66010 and then FUN_00e6d8f0 for the same cell.
The cell would remain valid between the two calls and no despawn branch would intervene.
evidence: FUN_00e78c00 contains mutually exclusive detach and rebuild branches.
FUN_00e6d8f0 has one direct caller, FUN_00e78c00, and is reached when +0x248 is already zero.
FUN_00e66010's callers are FUN_00e780a0, FUN_00e78c00, and FUN_00e7fd00; none is a proven straight-line same-cell detach-then-e6d8f0 pair.

hypotheses.name: despawn_releases_cell_identity
hypotheses.claim: FUN_00e780a0 is a despawn/transition boundary rather than a presentation-only refresh.
predictions: A matching sCellGame+0x411c should be cleared.
The old GFX record should be detached before the cell pool entry is released.
The cell pool release call should occur after the detach and optional replacement/child work.
evidence: FUN_00e780a0 clears +0x411c only on a match.
It calls FUN_00e66010 and conditionally FUN_00e67890/FUN_00e771d0.
It unconditionally calls FUN_00b72260(param_1) at the end.
It has 27 xrefs from 23 callers spanning death, interaction, population, and setup paths.

hypotheses.name: reload_discards_old_pool_identity
hypotheses.claim: Stage reload rebuilds runtime state from drained pools rather than refreshing the existing cells in place.
predictions: The avatar index should be cleared at reload entry.
Each old cCellObjectData should have its GFX association detached and then be released.
The body should perform later world/UI/setup work after the drain rather than reattaching the old cell records.
evidence: FUN_00e7fd00 sets sCellGame+0x411c to zero.
Its cell loop calls FUN_00e66010 and then FUN_00b72260 for each old pool index.
Its callers include the frame reload branch at 0x00e806b0 and cCellGame::Initialize.

hypotheses.name: content_identity_survives_gfx_association_changes
hypotheses.claim: mModelKey and mCellResource are content/resource ownership fields, not GFX handles.
predictions: CreateCellObject should populate +0xfc from GetModelKeyForCellResource and +0x108 from the resource reference.
GFX detach/rebuild should change +0x248 without clearing +0xfc or +0x108.
Effect/child/replacement helpers should resolve the resource through +0x108.
evidence: CreateCellObject writes the model key and resource reference.
FUN_00e66010 only clears +0x248 on the cell.
FUN_00e6d8f0, FUN_00e67890, and FUN_00e771d0 consume +0x108.
GetModelKeyForCellResource resolves through the cCellDataReference and writes a ResourceKey.

hypotheses.name: mode_service_teardown_is_separate_from_save
hypotheses.claim: OnExit and Dispose are service/mode cleanup boundaries, while cCellSerializableData is a separate in-memory save candidate.
predictions: OnExit should drain transient/presentation state without directly serializing the cell pool.
Dispose should release cCellGame, cCellGFX, and cCellUI through separate service paths.
cCellSerializableData should have its own 0xec allocation, vtables, and cCellGame+0x5190 ownership.
No direct disk transaction should be inferred from these teardown calls.
evidence: OnExit calls interaction/display/GFX/UI cleanup helpers and has no direct +0x411c/+0x108/+0x248 rewrite.
Dispose calls separate cCellGame, cCellGFX, and cCellUI teardown bodies.
FUN_00e61550 allocates 0xec bytes with serializable/refcount vtables; cCellGame+0x5190 owns mpSerializableData.
FUN_00e63d10 and FUN_00e819b0 show in-memory handoff/adoption, not a recovered disk write.

rules: Simulation identity is a stable CellId/pool index independent of presentation.
GFX association is optional, replaceable, and keyed by CellId; GFX/UI handles never become the simulation identity.
Model/content keys and resource references are separate from runtime resolved resource pointers and GFX handles.
Gameplay state remains authoritative in simulation; animation/pose/render output remains downstream.
Create, gameplay mutation, presentation detach, presentation rebuild, despawn, stage reload, OnExit, and Dispose are explicit lifecycle transitions.
cCellSerializableData is a separate mode-state DTO/candidate; live pool, GFX, UI, world, and resolved-resource handles are not presumed save-surviving.

resolved: The field ownership and the positive per-cell GFX detach/rebuild seam.
The negative result for retaining the old cell identity through FUN_00e780a0 and FUN_00e7fd00.
The separation of mModelKey/mCellResource, gameplay state, GFX/UI, and cCellSerializableData.
The distinction between per-cell GFX record rebuild and stage-level cCellGFX world/layer initialization.
not_resolved: Whether runtime callers always take the positive per-cell rebuild branch when a GFX association is absent.
The exact GFX pool reuse/sentinel behavior and hidden virtual-call retirement timing.
A runtime-observed detach -> rebuild sequence; this is a static observation only.
The complete cCellGFX::CellGFXObjectData layout because the imported structure exposes the pool but not the full record layout.
Complete cCellSerializableData field coverage, wire encoding, migration, and whether mode exit ever initiates a save.
